title: WPMS/1721/2017 of M/s Century Pulp And Paper Vs A.u Ansari AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1721 (M/S) of 2017
M/s Century Pulp and Paper ....... Petitioner
 versus
A.U. Ansari & others ....... Respondents
Mr. T.A. Khan, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Vinay Bhatt, Advocate for
the petitioner.
U.C. Dhyani, J. (Oral)
 By means of present writ petition, the
petitioner unit seeks following reliefs, among others:
(i) to issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the order dated
17.07.2017, passed by Civil Judge (Jr. Div.),
Haldwani, District Nainital in civil suit no. 27 of
2017 (Annexure 1 to the petition) so far it postpones
the hearing of application no. 6-C.
(ii) to issue suitable directions, restraining
the respondents from causing any hindrance in the
peaceful working of the unit of the petitioner at
Century Pulp and Paper, P.O. Ghanshyam Dham,
Lalkuan and also from blocking the egress and
ingress of the unit of the petitioner as well as
officers' and workers' colonies of the petitioners and
also from entering into the unit of the petitioner or
carrying any demonstration, dharna, sabha, meeting,
strike, hunger strike, procession etc. within a radius
of 200 meters from the outer periphery of the unit of
the petitioner and also from a distance of 200 meters

2
from all the gates of the unit of the petitioner as well
as from the gates going to the workers' and officers'
colony and also from causing obstruction in the
discharge of effluent from the unit of the petitioner.
2) In other words, the petitioner unit is
challenging the illegality and perversity of the order
dated 17.07.2017, passed by Civil Judge (Junior
Division), Haldwani, District Nainital, in civil suit no.
27 of 2017, by which the learned trial court refused to
grant ad-interim injunction in favour of the petitioner
and fixed the matter for 24.07.2017.
3) Normally, this Court would not have
entertained present writ petition and would have
relegated the petitioner unit to go back to the trial court
on the date already fixed by the court below. It has
been informed that 24.07.2017 is the date fixed before
the trial court. Law is clear on the point. Issuance of
notice is the rule. Grant of ad-interim injunction is the
exception. There is plethora of decisions on it.
4) What has compelled this Court to entertain
present writ petition is the fact that the respondents are
allegedly creating disturbance in their own campus.
Needless to say, that the workers have right to pursue
their lawful demands, although in a peaceful manner.
They can meet the management in furtherance of their
lawful demands, pursue them and have a meaningful

3
dialogue for amicable settlement, but they cannot be
permitted to sabotage public property and they also
cannot be permitted to take law in their own hands.
5) Learned Senior Counsel representing the
petitioner unit placed reliance upon the judgment
rendered by this Court in Writ Petition (M/S) no. 2647
of 2013 on 16.11.2013. Reliance is also placed upon
another judgment rendered by Hon'ble Madras High
Court in Writ Petition no. 18723 of 2003, decided on
12.06.2012, para 32 of which is as follows:
"32. By placing material evidence, the
petitioner has satisfied this Court for invoking
extraordinary remedy under Article 226 of the
Constitution of India. The only question to be
considered at this length of time is whether the
members of the union, respondents 4 to 11, have to
be kept away at a distance of 300 meters from the
factory premises to hold demonstrations, slogans or
conduct any of the lawful activities as per the Trade
Unions Act and other labour laws, permanently, by
issuance of a Mandamus. The contention that if they
have to stay away at a distance of 300 meters, and
even their voice would not be heard by the
Management deserves to be considered and having
regard to the rights granted under the Industrial
Laws to the workmen, and the rival contentions, this
Court is of the view that the Mandamus sought for
has to be granted, subject to a restriction of 200
meters from the factory premises, to hold dharna,
demonstration etc.
[emphasis supplied]
6) Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner
unit also relied upon the judgment rendered by the

4
Hon'ble High Court of Kerala in O.P. no. 2428 of 1997,
decided on 12.02.1997, para 7A of which is as follows:
"7A. In the above circumstances, I am satisfied
that the petitioner has revealed a perfect case for
direction to render police protection. Accordingly
the Respondents 2 to 4 are directed to render police
protection to the petitioner, at the petitioner's cost, in
the matter of free ingress and egress of the willing
workers, staff and managerial personnel, and also to
remove any finished and semi-finished goods from
the godown inside the factory premises and for free
movement of vehicles inside and outside the factory
premises. If there is any obstruction from the part of
striking workers such obstruction shall be removed
by the police. It is further made clear that the
protection granted shall not be made use of, either by
the management or by the police, to suppress any
peaceful agitation, resorted to by Respondents 6, 7
and 8 unions to pursue their demands."
[emphasis supplied]
7) In another judgment rendered by the
Hon'ble High Court of Kerala in W.A. no. 1 of 1994,
decided on 17.01.1994, it was observed that:
"16. Another contention raised by learned
counsel for the appellant was that, even if police
protection orders could be granted to prevent
violence, the management could not be allowed to
remove the finished or semi-finished products nor the
raw material in the factory especially when the
wages are unpaid. It must be noted here that, the
company had already incurred various obligations
under pending contracts to Indian and foreign

5
buyers, in respect of the finished products
manufactured. So far as semi-finished products and
raw material are concerned, they would get spoiled if
they are allowed to rot. As pointed out by the
learned Single Judge, the management may become
liable for damages and may lose future purchase
orders or export orders, as the case may be. The
management will have to pay income tax, municipal
taxes, excise duty, sales tax, electricity and water
charges, interest on borrowed monies, and other
levies during the financial year and if it had already
spent a large part of its funds for purchase of raw
material and if it has to pay for the above items, it
may, indeed, become bankrupt. Hence, the Court
cannot, while granting police protection as above,
impose restrictions that the company should not be
allowed to perform its contractual obligations
referred to above. The question as to whether and if
so, what wages are payable, has to be decided in the
various proceedings the workers or the management
may take under various Acts. It will be highly
disadvantageous if the performance of the
contractual and statutory obligations by the
employers is to be postponed till the completion of
the adjudication of these industrial disputes. If the
procedures under the various industrial or labour
laws otherwise permit, it will be open to the workmen
to adopt the said procedures to safeguard their
rights, or wages. In any event, the Company has its
other tangible assets sufficient to meet these financial
dues of the workmen, as and when the same are
determined by the appropriate courts, tribunals or
authorities."
 [emphasis supplied]
8) This Court would have, normally, issued
notices to the private respondents and, only then,
disposed of present writ petition, but since 24.07.2017
is the date already fixed before the trial court, therefore,
following order is passed in the interest of justice:

6
Respondents are directed to maintain law and
order in and around their own campus. They shall
not create hindrance in free ingress and egress of all
valid entrants. Obstructions, if any, coming in the
smooth and peaceful functioning of the petitioner unit
shall be got removed at the petitioner at its own cost.
These directions will not preclude agitators from
carrying on peaceful and lawful dharna or
demonstration without causing any hindrance in the
functioning of petitioner unit from a distance of 200
meters or more. Petitioner is also restrained from
suppressing peaceful agitation of the workers or
respondents to pursue their lawful demands.
9) This order shall hold good only upto
24.07.2017, the date fixed before the learned trial court.
10) Writ petition thus stands disposed of.

[Interim Relief application no. 8524 of 2017 is also
disposed of.]
11) Since present writ petition is being decided
without notice to the respondents, therefore, they are at
liberty to move for recall of this order, if they feel
aggrieved with the same.
 (U.C. Dhyani, J.)
